extracted.intended_audience: TikTok creators, social media marketers, and brands looking to increase reach and engagement on TikTok
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative criteria for creating TikTok videos likely to be recommended on the For You Page (FYP). Focuses on algorithmic signals, content production practices, posting cadence, and audience-building tactics for creators and marketers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement (likes, shares, saves, comments, watch time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement includes likes, shares, saves, comments and — perhaps most importantly — video watch time. TikTok uses these as signals that content is valuable and worth showing to more users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all engagement is equal: rewatching and sharing typically indicate stronger interest than a like or follow. High engagement with a small initial audience may prompt TikTok to test the video with a larger audience, but further boosts depend on how the next audiences react.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interactions (who the audience follows and engages with)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who a user follows and engages with influences the content they see on their For You Page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate followers who will meaningfully interact; cross-engagement (comments, profile visits) helps cement relevance signals to the algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video information and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Video details such as whether the content was created natively on TikTok, the video description (caption), and any embedded on-video text are used as signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize metadata by including chosen keywords in the video information, captions, and on-video text. Ensure the video content actually covers those keywords/queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device and account settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors like a user's location, language preference, and device type play a (less important) role in recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that some content may perform differently across regions or device types; localization and language cues can help reach target audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance signals and content restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok will not recommend certain content on the For You Page if it’s too graphic, endangers user safety, is tagged as 'not interested', or if the user has already seen it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow community guidelines, avoid flagged or repeat content, and design thumbnails and openings to avoid triggering 'not interested'.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok SEO (keyword research and optimization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat TikTok like a search engine: understand what your audience is searching for, identify 2–3 keywords that match common search terms, and optimize videos for those keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TikTok Creative Center and external keyword tools (Google Trends, Answer the Public, Exploding Topics). Weave keywords into captions, video info, and on-video text, and ensure the video answers the query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hashtag strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use relevant and trending hashtags to surface content to interested audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current best practice suggests 3–5 hashtags. Combine trending hashtags with evergreen ones relevant to your niche for broader and lasting discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use trending audio
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate trending sounds from TikTok’s library to increase discoverability and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor Creative Center and trending-sound tools; adopt trending audio while it’s still rising to catch momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use native TikTok features and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace TikTok-native functionality (filming in-app, Stitches, Duets, photo carousels) and native editing tools for better reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staying native can give an edge. Experiment with carousels, Stitches, Duets, and on-platform editing; consider CapCut for advanced editing that still feels native.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversation-starting captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions should invite interaction and include relevant keywords to help discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write captions that prompt comments or saves; sprinkle in keywords and a call-to-action (e.g., questions) to drive engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting frequency and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish TikTok videos consistently — ideally 3 to 5 times per week — to help the algorithm learn your style and capture trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buffer analysis shows posting 2–5 times/week yields ~17% increase in views per post, 6–10 times/week yields ~29%, and 11+ times/week yields ~34%. Do not sacrifice quality for quantity; skip a day rather than publish weak content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche down and run content series
rubrics_metrics.description: Honing in on a specific niche (and producing recurring content series) helps you reach a dedicated, target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define your niche clearly and consider series formats driven by follower suggestions or recurring themes to encourage repeat viewership and community growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance creativity with conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Create content that balances unique voice with what 'fits' on TikTok — content should look like what users expect on the app while still standing out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't copy-paste others; match familiar TikTok aesthetics or behaviors (raw, personal vibe) while injecting your unique perspective. High production is fine if it still feels personal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook quickly (TikTok’s 3-second rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: You have roughly three seconds to hook viewers — if you keep viewers engaged past three seconds, your chances of ranking on the FYP rise significantly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a strong visual or line, tease value immediately, and avoid slow intros that cause viewers to swipe away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize watch time and rewatch signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch time (and rewatches) are standout signals; lingering and rewatching can hugely affect what content is served to users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design videos that encourage full watches and replays (e.g., surprises, loops, information-dense content). Treat rewatches/saves/shares as higher-value engagement than likes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm testing and incremental exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok often shows a video to a small initial audience; if that audience reacts well, the platform tests it with larger groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for strong early engagement (from real, relevant viewers) to pass algorithmic tests; initial watch-time and reactions determine further distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use analytics to iterate
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze your TikTok analytics to see which videos are rewatched, shared, and watched at what times, and use those learnings to refine content strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track which topics, formats, times of day, and creative elements correlate with higher watch time and shares; double down on successful patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build community: engage, collaborate, leverage off-platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term growth depends on genuine connections: engage with followers, reply to comments, collaborate with other creators, and direct followers to other platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to comments, initiate collaborations—especially with complementary niches—and grow an email list or presence off-platform to diversify audience channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a recognizable signature or brand
rubrics_metrics.description: A consistent, recognizable element (visual or format) helps users immediately identify your content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a repeatable opener, color scheme, costume, or framing (example: showing laptop first) so repeat viewers recognize you and new viewers build expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize posting times
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting at times when your audience is most active can improve engagement and visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data-driven analyses (Buffer’s and other studies) to find best times but validate with your own audience analytics to determine personalized peak windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reset or retrain your For You Page
rubrics_metrics.description: You can’t completely wipe the slate, but you can refresh the For You feed and teach TikTok new preferences by adjusting content preferences and clearing histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: Profile → Settings and privacy → Content preferences → Refresh your For You feed; clear Watch history and Search history under Activity center; interact with content you want more of and press 'Not interested' on content you don't.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TikTok Creative Center and external research tools
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok Creative Center is a primary source for trending content, sounds, and rising creators; external tools supplement keyword and trend research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly consult Creative Center for rising trends and combine with tools like Google Trends, Answer the Public, and Exploding Topics to surface content ideas and keywords.
